newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin concerned by blast, warns Chechen leaders.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin concerned by blast, warns Chechen leaders.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday he was deeply concerned by the second explosion in five days on Russia's southern railway network and promised "decisive" measures to halt the suspected bomb attacks.

A Kremlin spokesman told Interfax news agency separatist leaders in Chechnya would be told to restore order in their region if a Chechen link was found in Monday's blast, which killed at least one person at a station in the Russian town of Pyatigorsk.
"The president...is extremely concerned by the terrorist act in Pyatigorsk and mourns for the innocent victims of the explosion," presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax.
Yeltsin, who is on holiday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi, will meet the governor of the Stavropol region which borders Chechnya to discuss law and order in the area on Tuesday, he said.

"If the law enforcement organs confirm a so-called 'Chechen link'...the government and Security Council Secretary Ivan Rybkin, on the president's oders, will have to warn the Grozny authorities about the need to establish order on the territory of their republic," Interfax said, quoting Yastrzhembsky.

Russian officials said they suspected a Chechen link in the blast, five days after a bomb killed two people at a railway station in Armavir, also in southern Russia. Chechen leaders in their capital, Grozny, denied any role in either indicdent.
